347	/**
348	 * Fold a branch onto a base world and hand back the second world.
349	 *
350	 * Both worlds are drawn in one coordinate space afterwards, so nothing here
351	 * moves a claim: the union of the two maps is laid out once and painted twice.
352	 *
353	 * @param base The base world, exactly as the map was written.
354	 * @param branch The branch: its edits in order, and whatever whole claims and
355	 *   arrows the map supplied for them.
356	 * @param engine Where the engine has got to. Once it has answered, its claims
357	 *   carry the computed likelihoods, its badges are read off the world, and its
358	 *   difference says which claims moved. While it is still being asked, the room
359	 *   those answers will take is reserved and says why it is empty.
360	 */
361	export function branchWorld(base: WorldView, branch: BranchView, engine?: Engine): WorldView {
362	  const computed = answered(engine);
363	  // The claims and arrows to draw. With the engine, they are the map its edits
364	  // left behind — which already holds whatever the branch added. Without it,
365	  // the base map plus whatever whole claims and arrows the branch supplied.
366	  const claims = computed === undefined ? [...base.claims, ...branch.claims] : computed.now.claims;
367	  const links = computed === undefined ? [...base.links, ...branch.links] : computed.now.links;
368	  const diff = readDiff(
369	    claims.map((claim) => claim.id),
370	    asArrows(links),
371	    branch.edits,
372	  );
373	
374	  const words = new Map(claims.map((claim) => [claim.id, claim.claim]));
375	  for (const edit of branch.edits) {
376	    if (edit.op === "insert" && !words.has(edit.claimId)) {
377	      words.set(edit.claimId, edit.words);
378	    }
379	  }
380	  // What the tiles say about the edits behind them. With the engine, the world
381	  // carries every value an edit fixed and every supposition a later edit
382	  // undermined, and the badges were read off it; without it they are derived
383	  // here from the branch. One line, one derivation, whichever it is.
384	  const derived = badgesByClaim(branch.edits, {
385	    words,
386	    arrows: new Map(
387	      branch.links.map((link) => [
388	        link.id,
389	        { source: link.source, mode: link.mode, strength: link.strength },
390	      ]),
391	    ),
392	  });
393	  const badges =
394	    computed === undefined
395	      ? derived
396	      : new Map(computed.now.claims.map((claim) => [claim.id, [...(claim.badges ?? [])]]));
397	  const standing =
398	    computed === undefined
399	      ? standingByClaim(branch.edits, derived)
400	      : new Map(
401	          computed.now.claims.flatMap((claim) =>
402	            claim.standing === undefined ? [] : [[claim.id, claim.standing] as const],
403	          ),
404	        );
405	
406	  // Your own numbers, from every **My own number** edit on this branch. A later
407	  // one on the same claim replaces an earlier one on screen; both stay in the
408	  // branch, in order, because the branch is the audit trail.
409	  const yours = new Map(
410	    branch.edits.flatMap((edit) => (edit.op === "believe" ? [[edit.target, edit.belief]] : [])),
411	  );
412	
413	  return {
414	    ...base,
415	    ...(computed === undefined
416	      ? {}
417	      : {
418	          // How the engine was run, so the chip can say whether its range was
419	          // computed and the line under the map can name the seed.
420	          versions: computed.now.versions,
421	          worldsPerVersion: computed.now.worldsPerVersion,
422	          seed: computed.now.seed,
423	          warnings: computed.now.warnings,
424	        }),
425	    branch,
426	    claims: claims.map((claim): ClaimView => {
427	      const ownNumber = yours.get(claim.id);
428	      const structural = diff.states.get(claim.id) ?? "untouched";
429	      const state = tileState(structural, computed?.change, claim.id);
430	      // How far the number moved — unless the claim is standing on the reader's
431	      // own say-so, in which case there is no number to have moved to. While a
432	      // supposition holds the claim is true in every version of the map, and the
433	      // engine stores a flat 1 on it so that a chain has a factor to multiply;
434	      // **no surface prints that number**, and a reading of ".40 up to >.99" is
435	      // that number wearing the certainty guard's clothes. The badge pair says
436	      // *Supposed · Oct 1* instead, which is what actually happened.
437	      const supposed = standing.get(claim.id) !== undefined;
438	      // What the engine read on this claim: the two numbers, which way they
439	      // went, and whether the move came from nothing but the observation
440	      // changing how much each version counts. It is carried for **every** claim
441	      // the engine read, not only the ones it calls `shifted` — a claim can move
442	      // a hair and still come out unchanged, and when it did so purely by
443	      // reweighting the panel has a sentence for exactly that.
444	      const moved = supposed ? undefined : computed?.change.claims.get(claim.id)?.moved;
445	      // Which tiles reserve a line for how far their number moved: the ones the
446	      // edit can reach, and only those. A claim it added, one it forced false
447	      // and one it cannot reach have nothing to say there, and a claim standing
448	      // on the reader's say-so says the word instead. **The same set in both
449	      // states**, so the tile is the same size before and after the answer.
450	      const reserves = (state === "downstream" || state === "shifted") && !supposed;
451	      return {
452	        ...claim,
453	        diff: state,
454	        moved,
455	        badges: [
456	          ...(badges.get(claim.id) ?? []),
457	          // The tile's line reads the move only when the engine calls the claim
458	          // shifted. A claim that moved a hair and came out unchanged reads *no
459	          // change*, which is the engine's own verdict; the two numbers behind
460	          // it are one click away in the panel.
461	          ...(reserves && engine !== undefined

8	 * drift from the other.

10	 * **There is no arithmetic anywhere in this file.** A likelihood is read from
11	 * the server and carried, untouched and at full precision, to the component that
12	 * prints it. Rounding is a display decision and is made once, in the chip.
13	 *

16	 * function below that hands back a blank, a zero or a stand-in.

39	/**
40	 * The seed every question about one map is asked with.
41	 *
42	 * A world can always be rebuilt from three things — the map, the branch and the
43	 * seed — so the seed has to be the same on every visit, or the same map would
44	 * read differently twice in a row. It is read off the map's own date rather than
45	 * picked: the stored example is set on 2026-10-01, so the seed is 20261001. It
46	 * is printed under the map, beside the map's address, so that anybody can ask
47	 * the engine the same question and get the same answer.
48	 *
49	 * A seed is an input, not a reading. Nothing on screen is a number this
50	 * produced; it decides which of two thousand versions of the map get tried.
51	 *
52	 * @param bundle The stored example in full.
53	 * @returns The map's own date with its dashes taken out, as a whole number.
54	 */
55	export function seedFor(bundle: FixtureBundle): number {
56	  return Number(bundle.fixture_date.replaceAll("-", ""));
57	}
58	
59	/**
60	 * Turn a likelihood from the server into a filled slot, unchanged.
61	 *
62	 * The three numbers are copied across at full precision. Rounding is a display
63	 * decision and is made once, in the chip that prints them.
64	 */
65	export function filled(belief: Belief): Known<Ranged> {
66	  return { reading: { p: belief.p, lo: belief.lo, hi: belief.hi } };
67	}

69	/** Turn "there is no number here" into the words and the reason for them. */
70	export function missing(kind: AbsenceKind, words: string, reason: string): Known<Ranged> {
71	  const absence: Absence = { kind, words, reason };
72	  return { absence };
73	}

75	/**
76	 * The single letter that stands for a publication, taken from the host name in
77	 * its own web address.
78	 *
79	 * `https://www.bbc.com/news/...` gives `B`. A leading `www.` is dropped first,
80	 * because every publication has one and it would make every monogram a `W`.
81	 *
82	 * A letter rather than the publication's own icon, deliberately: an icon is a
83	 * request to somebody else's server, and this app draws its first frame without
84	 * making one.
85	 */

87	  let host: string;
88	  try {
89	    host = new URL(url).hostname;
90	  } catch {

92	    // to show, and the mark beside it says plainly that there is no host name.
93	    return { monogram: "?", host: "an address we could not read" };
94	  }
95	  const withoutWww = host.startsWith("www.") ? host.slice(4) : host;

100	/** Turn one published item into the clipping a tile shows. */
101	function clipping(evidence: Evidence): EvidenceClipping {
102	  const { monogram, host } = monogramFor(evidence.url);
103	  return {
104	    line: evidence.claim,

106	    host,

147	 */

149	  proposition: Proposition,

152	  if (stored === null || stored === undefined) {

159	    };
160	  }
161	  return {
162	    reading: {
163	      referenceClass: stored.reference_class,
164	      k: stored.k,
165	      n: stored.n,
166	      sources: stored.sources.map((url) => source({ url, title: url, retrieved: null })),

169	}

171	/**
172	 * Why a claim has no market number, in the words the shared vocabulary settles.
173	 *

175	 * the tile and the panel beside the map cannot drift apart about what "no

189	/** Why this claim has no market number. */

205	 * What stands where a chain's multiplied-out likelihood would go.
206	 *
207	 * **A world does not carry one yet.** It holds a likelihood for every claim and
208	 * a series for every day, and nothing anywhere multiplies a route's steps
209	 * together. The engine will carry it; until it does the slot says so, because
210	 * working it out here would put a second answer on the map beside the engine's.
211	 */
212	export const NO_PATH_PRODUCT: Absence = {
213	  kind: "no_engine",
214	  words: "no engine yet",
215	  reason:
216	    "Nothing has multiplied this chain out. The likelihood of a whole route is worked out " +
217	    "where the map's numbers are, and the engine does not carry one yet.",
218	};

242	      user: beliefs.user

244	        : missing("not_said", "—", "You have not put your own number on this claim yet."),

278	    mode: link.mode,
279	    // Carried across at full precision and never touched. The wire compares it

def _days_to_work_out(
    claims: Mapping[PropositionId, Proposition], day_zero: date, days: int
) -> NDArray[numpy.int64]:
    """Choose which days of the window to work the numbers out on.

    Ordinarily every day. Past 180 days that is more points than anybody scrubs
    through, so the series is drawn at 180 evenly spaced days instead — **and every
    claim's own resolve-by day is always among them**. That is not a nicety: a
    tile's headline number is read on the claim's own resolve-by day, and if that
    day were not on the claim's own series the number on the tile would not be a
    point of the line drawn beneath it.

    Args:
        claims: Every claim on the map, by identifier.
        day_zero: The day the window starts on.
        days: How long the window is.

    Returns:
        The days to work out, in order.
    """
    judged = numpy.array(
        sorted({_day_index(one.resolution.by, day_zero, days) for one in claims.values()}),
        dtype=numpy.int64,
    )
    if days + 1 <= SERIES_CAP:
        return numpy.arange(days + 1, dtype=numpy.int64)
    spare = max(2, SERIES_CAP - len(judged))
    evenly = numpy.rint(numpy.linspace(0, days, spare)).astype(numpy.int64)
    return numpy.union1d(judged, evenly).astype(numpy.int64)
